summary: Manfred Mayrhofer was a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Graz under Wilhelm Brandenstein, later holding posts at Würzburg, Saarland, Vienna, and the Austrian Academy of Sciences.
Manfred Steger works in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Rutgers University and under Robert Aitken, and held a post at RMIT University from approximately 2003 to 2014.
Manfred Taube was a Tibetologist who studied under Friedrich Weller from around 1947 to 1957. In 1991, he held a professorship in Central Asian studies at Leipzig University.

Manshi Kiyozawa was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Toyo University and the University of Tokyo under Ernest Fenollosa. He served as principal of Kyoto Prefectural Rakuhoku and later as president of Otani University.
Manudeva was an Indologist and linguist. He studied under traditional teacher Bālakṛṣṇa Pāyaguṇḍa and disciple Bāla Śarman Pāyaguṇḍe.

Marc Aurel Stein was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Leipzig, Vienna, and Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, he held leadership posts at Oriental College, Lahore, Aliah University, and the Archaeological Survey of India.

Marc Tiefenauer is an Indology scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Lausanne under Johannes Bronkhorst, with Christine Chojnacki and Vincent Eltschinger on his committee, and also studied under Nahid Rouzbeh.

Marc-Henri Deroche specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral studies under Matthew T. Kapstein and studied under scholars including Fernand Meyer, Samten Gyaltsen Karmay, Katsumi Mimaki, Heather Stoddard, and Franz-Karl Ehrhard.

Marcel Granet was a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who studied at École Normale Supérieure and under Édouard Chavannes. He held posts at the EPHE, INALCO, Institut des Hautes Études Chinoises, and Collège de France.

Marcel Mauss worked in religious studies. After studying at the University of Bordeaux, he held academic posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from around 1901 to 1940 and the Collège de France from 1931 to 1942.

Marcelle Lalou was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Paris under Sylvain Lévi, Jacques Bacot, and Paul Pelliot, and later held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études.

Marco Walther is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich under doctoral supervisor Franz-Karl Ehrhard and committee member Jens-Uwe Hartmann.

Marcus Bingenheimer specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Educated at Nagoya University and the University of Würzburg under Norbert Klaes, he held posts at Chung-Hwa Institute, Dharma Drum institutions, and Temple University.

Marek Mejor is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He held a post as professor at the University of Warsaw from circa 1976 to 2002 and was a junior research fellow at Wolfson College, Oxford, in 1981–1982.

Marek Zemánek is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Dongguk University, Seoul National University, and completed his dissertation at Charles University under the supervision of Radek Chlup.

Margaret Dornish worked in religious studies and Sinology. She studied at Yale University, the University of Southern California, and Claremont Graduate University, and was an Associate Professor of Religion at Pomona College from around 1969.
Margaret Gouin specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed her PhD at the University of Bristol between 2002 and 2006 under the supervision of Paul Williams.

Margaret Mead was an academic who studied at DePauw University, Barnard College, and Columbia University. She held long-term posts at the American Museum of Natural History and Columbia University, and also held a post at the University of Rhode Island.

Margaret R. Miles is a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology. She studied at San Francisco State University and the Graduate Theological Union, and served on the faculty at Harvard University and Harvard Divinity School from 1978 to 1996.

Margarita Angelica Delgado Creamer specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Pittsburgh under Linda Penkower and completed postdoctoral work under Xiuping Hong.
